hero.subtitle: Our project management internship teaches you to take an IT project from idea to delivery. You write charters, build schedules and budgets, run Agile sprints in Jira and manage risk on real projects, with a 1:1 mentor from Icanio.

answer.question: What is the project management internship at Icanio Tech School?
answer.answer: It is a mentored program where students learn how IT projects are planned and delivered at Icanio Technologies. You cover the project lifecycle, scope, schedules, budgets, Agile and Scrum, risk and stakeholder communication, then present a capstone. The project management internship runs from 15 days to six months, offline or online, and ends with a certificate.

sections.heading: What a project manager does, and why every team needs one
sections.intro: A project manager makes sure the right people do the right work at the right time, within budget. In IT, that means turning a client's goal into a plan a team can deliver.
paragraphs: Software projects have many moving parts. Designers, developers, testers and clients all depend on each other. Without someone watching the whole picture, deadlines slip, costs grow and small problems turn into big ones.

A project manager defines what is in and out of scope, breaks the work into tasks, builds a schedule and tracks progress. They also run meetings, report status, manage risks and handle changes. Much of the job is communication: keeping everyone informed and aligned.

Every IT company, from a small startup to a large services firm, needs people with these skills. Many freshers start as project coordinators or Scrum team members and grow into managers. That is why a project management internship with real projects is valuable. It teaches the habits hiring managers look for before they trust you with a team.
At Icanio Technologies, project managers run delivery for client products every week. Our project management internship puts you inside that rhythm, from kickoff to the final retrospective.
bullets: Define scope and objectives with a project charter
Break work into tasks and build a realistic timeline
Run sprints, stand-ups and reviews with an Agile team
Track risks, changes and status for stakeholders

sections.heading: Who should join the project management internship?
sections.intro: You do not need to code. You need organisation, clear communication and a calm head under deadlines. These four groups get the most from our project management internship.

items.title: Fresh graduates
items.body: You want to enter IT, operations or business teams with a structured, practical skill set that employers recognise.

items.title: Career switchers
items.body: You work in another field and want to move into a project management role with hands-on practice behind you.

items.title: Junior team leads
items.body: You already guide a small team and want to formalise your planning, tracking and delivery skills.

items.title: Entrepreneurs
items.body: You run a startup or side project and need to manage several timelines, tasks and people at once.

sections.heading: Project management internship curriculum in 4 phases
sections.intro: Each phase of the project management internship ends with a plan, board or report your mentor reviews. Shorter durations cover the early phases; three and six month interns finish all four and present a capstone.

items.label: Phase 1
items.title: Foundations of project management
points: What project management is, and what makes a project succeed
The project lifecycle: initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, closure
Roles and responsibilities of a project manager in an IT team
Project initiation and writing a project charter
Defining scope, objectives and success criteria

items.label: Phase 2
items.title: Planning and scheduling
points: Work breakdown structure (WBS) for a real project
Gantt charts and project timelines
Resource planning and allocation
Budget estimation and cost control
Dependency mapping and the critical path

items.label: Phase 3
items.title: Agile, Scrum and execution
points: Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery, and when each fits
Scrum ceremonies: planning, daily stand-up, review and retrospective
Kanban boards and backlog management
Risk identification, a risk register and mitigation plans
Stakeholder communication plans

items.label: Phase 4
items.title: Delivery, closure and career preparation
points: Project monitoring and weekly status reports
Change management fundamentals and change requests
Project closure and lessons learned
Capstone project presentation to a panel
PM resume and interview coaching

sections.heading: How our project management internship builds real habits
sections.intro: You cannot learn to manage a project from slides. You learn it when a task slips, a client changes their mind and you have to respond.
paragraphs: Every project management internship student manages a real or realistic project from start to finish. You write the charter, build the WBS and schedule, and set up the Jira board. Then you run it. Your mentor joins stand-ups and reviews, and watches how you handle blockers.

Partway through, your mentor introduces a change: a new feature request, a team member on leave or a budget cut. You update the plan, raise a change request and explain the impact to the stakeholder. This is the part of the job textbooks rarely cover.

Each week you send a short status report. Your mentor returns it with comments on clarity, tone and honesty. In our experience, a clear status report that flags risks early earns more trust than a perfect-looking plan.
By the end of the project management internship, you will have a complete project file that shows how you planned, adapted and delivered.

Send weekly status reports with mentor feedback

sections.heading: What you will achieve in the project management internship

items.body: A charter, scope statement, WBS, Gantt chart, resource plan and budget for one project, reviewed by an Icanio mentor.

items.title: Risk and change control

items.title: Stakeholder communication

sections.heading: What your capstone project file should include
sections.intro: Recruiters want proof that you can plan and deliver. Our mentors help you assemble the file from your project management internship so it tells a clear story.
items: A one-page project charter with scope, objectives and success criteria
A WBS and Gantt chart showing dependencies and the critical path
A resource plan and budget with a simple cost tracker in Excel
A Jira or Trello board with sprints, backlog and completed work
A risk register and at least one handled change request
Weekly status reports and a closure note with lessons learned

faqs.q: Is a tech background needed for a project management internship?
faqs.a: No. You do not write code as a project manager. It helps to understand how software is built, and Phase 1 covers that in plain terms. What matters most is organisation, clear writing and staying calm when plans change. Our team checks your background when you apply and suggests a duration.

faqs.q: Who can apply for the project management internship?
faqs.a: Engineering, BCA, MCA, B.Com, BBA and MBA students can all apply, as can recent graduates and working professionals. Junior team leads and founders who want to formalise their planning skills also join. If you have led a college event or club, you already have useful instincts to build on.

faqs.q: Which tools will I learn in the project management internship?
faqs.a: You will use MS Project for schedules and timelines, Jira for Agile tracking, Trello for Kanban boards, Confluence for team documentation, MS Excel for budgets and reports, and Slack for team communication. You also learn Gantt charts, WBS and risk registers as working methods.

faqs.q: How long is the project management internship?
faqs.a: You choose from 15 days up to six months. A short project management internship covers foundations and planning. Three and six month internships cover all four phases, including Agile execution, change control and closure, and finish with a capstone presentation that makes a much stronger portfolio.

faqs.q: Does the project management internship cover Scrum?
faqs.a: Yes. Phase 3 covers Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery, Scrum ceremonies and roles, Kanban and backlog management. You then run real sprints in Jira during your project. Our team recommends reading the official Scrum Guide alongside the internship so the terms stay clear.

faqs.q: Do I get a certificate after the internship?
faqs.a: Yes. Every intern who completes the project management internship receives an Icanio Tech School certificate stating the track and duration. More useful in interviews is your project file, which shows your charter, schedule, board, risk register and status reports in one place.

faqs.q: Can I do the project management internship online?
faqs.a: Yes. You can attend offline at our centre in Tirunelveli, join online, or choose part-time weekday or weekend batches. Stand-ups and reviews work well over video, and all your plans and boards live in shared tools like Jira, Confluence and Slack.

faqs.q: What jobs follow a project management internship?
faqs.a: Common entry roles are project coordinator, associate project manager, Scrum team member, PMO analyst and delivery coordinator. Top performers from the project management internship are referred to the Icanio talent team. Every intern also gets resume review, LinkedIn guidance and interview coaching.

takeaways: The project management internship at Icanio Tech School covers foundations, planning, Agile and delivery in 4 phases.
You use MS Project, Jira, Trello, Confluence, Excel and Slack on a real project.
A mid-project change request and weekly status reports build habits textbooks miss.
The project management internship runs from 15 days to six months, offline, online or part time, with 1:1 mentorship.
You finish with a full project file, a certificate and a possible referral to Icanio Technologies.
conclusion: Project management is learned by running a project, adapting when things change and explaining the result. Our project management internship gives you that practice, with mentors who deliver client projects every week.
If you want to plan and lead work in tech, apply today. Our team will help you choose a duration and start date that fits your college schedule.
